_comment: There is DELIBERATELY no permissions.deny list here for tenant commands.
This file is committed, so it is read by every checkout of this repo —
including the tenant ops worktree, whose entire job is running those very
commands. A deny rule cannot tell the two apart: it is static, it matches
by prefix, and deny beats allow, so `Bash(npm run migrate:amadiya)` here
would block the one workspace that is supposed to run it, while still
missing `node supabase/migrate.mjs --env=amadiya` in this one (the danger
is in the MIDDLE of that command, and prefix rules cannot see it).
The PreToolUse hook below does both jobs properly: it matches on patterns
rather than prefixes, and it derives which workspace it is running in from
whether a kind:'tenant' env file is present. See CLAUDE.md, first section.
Neither is the actual boundary. The boundary is that .env.amadiya.local
does not exist in the development checkout, so nothing there can
authenticate as the tenant however many rules are bypassed.
